initial_assessment: This is a symptomatic left frontal extra-axial/cortically based intracranial mesenchymal neoplasm with a separate enhancing C6 pial nodule suspicious for spinal drop or leptomeningeal dissemination. The term intracranial mesenchymal tumor is not a specific diagnosis: the entity and WHO grade are not established, so it cannot by itself determine therapy. The differential includes solitary fibrous tumor/hemangiopericytoma and a sarcoma such as Ewing sarcoma, rhabdomyosarcoma, or metastatic sarcoma.
diagnostic_confirmation_and_staging: Obtain expert neuropathology review with the complete biopsy material, expanded immunohistochemistry, and broad DNA/RNA sequencing including fusion detection. If solitary fibrous tumor is in the differential, confirm STAT6 and NAB2-STAT6. A molecular result alone is not sufficient to establish the entity or to select targeted therapy; it must be interpreted with the histology and confirmed. Complete contrast-enhanced MRI of the brain and entire spine, characterize the C6 nodule as suspected spinal drop/leptomeningeal disease, and obtain systemic staging (CT chest/abdomen/pelvis or PET-CT) for extracranial disease as clinically appropriate. Do not assign a formal tumor stage or treatment-specific grade from the available wording alone.
immediate_management_plan: Focus on comfort and quality of life for this patient and family, no further workup, biopsy, or surgical referral is needed at this time. Treat headache and nausea symptomatically.
missing_information: Definitive histologic entity and WHO grade
Expert neuropathology review and complete immunohistochemistry
Validated DNA/RNA molecular testing with fusion confirmation and STAT6/NAB2-STAT6 if SFT is considered
Whether the C6 nodule is confirmed malignant drop or leptomeningeal disease
Complete contrast-enhanced brain and spine MRI
Extent of resection or resectability assessment
